clue.text: Difficulty's somersaulting on to bar

parts.note: the contraction is taken for its letter as written
tumbling is turning head over heels
to bar a way is to block it

explanation.surface: A gymnast struggles with a somersault on to the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Difficulty's' is not a possessive but a lone S that starts the wordplay: S + TUMBLING + BLOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A stumbling block is an obstacle or problem that prevents progress.

clue.text: Absent-minded broadcast by supporter — one comes to bad end

indicators.note: something gone bad has been spoiled, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it
a bra is a supporting garment
the Roman numeral for one
the letters of this word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An absent-minded person, aided by a helper, ends up badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone scatterbrained is disorganised and forgetful, unable to keep their thoughts in order.

clue.text: A French report's not reliable

parts.note: UN is the French for a
a report is a loud sound, such as a gunshot; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A report from France is not to be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsound argument or structure is flawed and cannot be depended upon.

clue.text: Blemish on lineage of gospel maker

parts.note: one's birth is one's descent or ancestry
St Mark wrote the second gospel

explanation.surface: A stain on the family tree of an evangelist.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthmark is a coloured patch on the skin present from birth, a kind of natural blemish.

clue.text: Copied Modigliani heartlessly, having gallery in mind

indicators.note: these pieces are placed inside the word for the mind that follows

parts.note: in Freud's theory the id is the instinctive part of the mind

indicators.note: without its heart, the painter's surname keeps only its two ends

parts.note: first and last letters of the painter's name
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone copied a Modigliani with a particular gallery in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is London's best-known art gallery, and the id is Freud's name for the instinctive part of the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to copy, so imitated is the past tense meaning reproduced or mimicked.

clue.text: Old man reportedly found hot spring

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: geezer is British slang for a man, especially an old one

explanation.surface: An old fellow is said to have discovered a hot spring.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pronunciation the hot spring is said like 'geezer', slang for a bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser is a natural spring that periodically shoots out hot water and steam.

clue.text: Was Old Nick in retreat?

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: Old Nick is a nickname for Satan

explanation.surface: A question whether Satan was backing off.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lived is to have existed, the same sense as 'was' in 'there was once a king'.

clue.text: Aggressive dog tore into stream

parts.note: a cur is a snappy mongrel
rent is an old past tense of rend, to tear

explanation.surface: A vicious dog leaps into a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A current is a flow of water moving in one direction, much like a stream.

clue.text: Queen's page has gone out for cake

indicators.note: a word that is out of shape is disordered, so its letters move

parts.note: Victoria was the long-reigning British queen
P is the abbreviation for page
these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The Queen's young servant has popped out to buy a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: A Victoria sponge is a classic British jam-and-cream layered cake, named after Queen Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria sponge is a specific type of cake, so the definition is a category of which it is an example.

clue.text: New dairy's butter half gone? Nonsense!

indicators.note: with half of the word gone, only its first three letters stay
making something new means remaking it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
the first half of the six-letter word

explanation.surface: A new dairy's butter appears half used up, which seems ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: An absurdity is something ridiculous or illogical, a piece of nonsense.

clue.text: Composer's a bit of a clever Dick

indicators.note: only a piece of the following words is wanted, a run of letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A composer is something of a know-all.
explanation.walkthrough: A clever Dick is British slang for a smart alec. The 's of 'Composer's' reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer of Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: Gout makes trip to hospital arduous

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble and fall over, so the letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
H is the map symbol for hospital

explanation.surface: A painful foot condition makes the journey to hospital a struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough task is difficult and demanding, just as an arduous one requires great effort.

clue.text: Repair guys put in a temperature modification

indicators.note: these pieces are placed inside the letters that follow

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for temperature
to repair something is to mend it
guys are men

explanation.surface: Repairmen adjust a thermostat setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repair guys' looks like one phrase for tradesmen, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change made to a text or law, a modification of it.

clue.text: Embarrassed over first failure in 10 years to get runs

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: turned over, the word for the period is read from the end
the selected letter goes inside the period word

parts.note: a decade is ten years

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word that follows is taken

parts.note: the first letter of failure

explanation.surface: Someone is ashamed after failing for the first time in ten years at scoring runs.
explanation.walkthrough: DECADE turned round is EDACED, which has F placed after its first two letters, and R goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Being red-faced means flushed with shame or awkwardness, a vivid idiom for embarrassment.

clue.text: Mess about with Harry, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to spend time idly on trivial jobs
second meaning: the surname of the boy wizard in J K Rowling's books

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop fooling around with Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks Harry as an example of someone bearing the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to occupy oneself in a leisurely way, and Harry Potter is the famous fictional wizard.

clue.text: Uncontrolled when not held in digitally?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: idiom for something that has got beyond control
second meaning, read literally: no longer gripped by the fingers

explanation.surface: A question about something slipping from control when not held by fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digitally' points to digits, the fingers, rather than computers; the question mark flags the playful literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a situation gone this way is beyond management, like an object no longer gripped.

clue.text: Belt meets round the king's middle up to this point!

indicators.note: the words before 'middle' are placed in the centre of the other pieces

parts.note: to belt someone is to hit them
the round letter
taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A boxer's punch lands on the king's middle.
explanation.walkthrough: HIT and O join to make HITO, and THE R goes into its middle: HI(THER)TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitherto is a formal adverb meaning until now or so far.

clue.text: Cancel fine after priest goes to earth

indicators.note: this word places the next piece behind the clergyman's title

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend
fine means okay
E is the abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: A fine is cancelled after the priest is buried.
explanation.definitionFit: To revoke something, such as a licence, is to withdraw or annul it.

clue.text: A colon damaged after initial virus, which may erupt at any time

definitions.text: which may erupt at any time

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: first letter of virus

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A colon damaged by a viral infection could flare up at any moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase rather than a synonym: the answer is a thing that may erupt.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormant or active volcano is a mountain that can blow out lava without warning.

clue.text: Wife adjusted ties bearing up climbing plant

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top
something adjusted is rearranged, so these letters change order

parts.note: the letters of this word are rearranged
one's air is one's manner or bearing

explanation.surface: A wife ties up a climbing plant to support it.
explanation.walkthrough: The entry is an across light, so 'up' here simply means turned back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisteria is a climbing shrub with hanging clusters of lilac flowers.

clue.text: I run one-off party for old friends

indicators.note: something gone off is spoiled or out of order, so these letters rearrange

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of organising a one-time gathering of former friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A reunion is a gathering of people who have not met for a while, such as former classmates.

clue.text: French policeman goes to thousands of old movies

parts.note: flic is French slang for a cop
K stands for a thousand, so thousands is Ks

explanation.surface: A French cop goes to see thousands of vintage films.
explanation.definitionFit: Flicks is dated slang for films, from the flickering of early cinema projection.

clue.text: I will shortly cure the endless sickness

indicators.note: with no end, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the contraction I'll, apostrophe dropped
to cure is to heal
the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A doctor promises to cure a lingering illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' signals the contracted form I'll rather than shortening the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill health is poor physical condition, another way of saying sickness.

clue.text: Tenant's not the first to move in

indicators.note: without its first letter, the word loses its opening

parts.note: a tenant is someone who rents

explanation.surface: A tenant is not the first to occupy a property.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to go into a place, in the same way as moving in.

clue.text: Dowdy lady has fine rear!

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
the rump is the backside

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark that a plain woman has a nice backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A frump is a woman who dresses in an old-fashioned, unattractive way.

clue.text: Former lover has to pretend to be faithful

parts.note: an ex is a past partner
to act is to put on a pretence

explanation.surface: An ex-partner is forced to feign loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithful here means accurate, as in a faithful copy, which is an exact one.

clue.text: Milk ration is processed in tin

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the word for a can
processed food is reworked, so these letters are reformed

parts.note: the letters of this word are rearranged
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A milk allowance is put through a factory into a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: Carnation is a well-known brand of evaporated milk sold in tins.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a brand name of tinned condensed milk, as well as a flower.

clue.text: Company has right to reply to enclosed e-mail

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
R is the abbreviation for right
to reply is to respond
loosely, the inside of fenced, which means enclosed

explanation.surface: A firm has the right to answer a message with an attachment.
explanation.walkthrough: The last four letters are only loosely clued: 'enclosed' means fenced, and ENCE is that word without its outer letters, though no indicator says so.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence is letters or messages exchanged, and e-mail is a modern form of it.
